vm Virtual Machine > CLI Usage in Detail

CLI Usage in Detail

This page explains, item by item, all command-line arguments, optional environment variables, and typical run modes for sa vm run and sa vm test. After reading this section you will be able to assemble any interpreted-execution command you want, and understand how each mode affects the return code.

Usage Skeleton

The complete usage definition for the vm subcommand is in src/plugin.zig::usageText(), reproduced here:

Usage: sa vm <run|test> [--allow-ffi] [--sandboxed] [--stats] [--profile=N]
           [--policy=<file.json>] [--fuel=N] [--deadline-ms=N]
           [--mem-cap-bytes=N] [--max-call-depth=N] <file.sa|.sab>

The positional argument must be .sa / .sal source or a .sab bytecode module. Whether the input is SAB or source is decided by whether the first 4 bytes match the SAB magic ("SAB\x00"), not by the extension — you could also name a .sa file with any suffix as long as the first 4 bytes are correct (not recommended; the extension takes precedence).

Parsing order: first consume argv[0]=="sa", argv[1]=="vm", then require argv[2] ∈ {run, test}. After that, scan options starting from argv[3]; the first token that does not start with -- is treated as file_path, and parsing of the remaining flags stops.

Subcommands

NameBehaviorSource of return code
runParse and execute; if the source has no @main, fall back to @test modeThe return value of @main (truncated to u8)
testIterate over all @test functions and execute them one by one in lexicographic orderReturns 0 if all pass; any panic terminates with 128 + (code & 0x7f)
NoteThe two subcommands share the same parsing / sandbox / entry point inside vm; the only difference is “look for @main versus look for all @test”.

Flags

FlagSyntaxBehaviorExit / side effects
--allow-ffiStands alone, no valueSets FfiManager.allow_ffi to true; the 4 raw libc symbols dlopen/dlsym/dlclose/dlerror are only then returned in resolveSymbolConflicts with --sandboxed; combined use directly yields E_SANDBOX_MISCONFIG → exit 234
--sandboxedStands alone, no valueLoads the built-in default-deny policy given by policy_mod.parseSandboxed(allocator)Simultaneously forbids --allow-ffi and --policy; a conflict yields E_SANDBOX_MISCONFIG → exit 234
--statsStands alone, no valueAfter execution, prints the “VM stats:” block to stderrDoes not affect the exit code
--profile=N--profile=10 or --profile 10Includes everything in --stats, plus a Top N function table sorted by inclusive time0 is not allowed (parse failure → exit 1)
--policy=path--policy=foo.json or --policy foo.jsonLoads a sa.vm.policy/1 policy from JSONPolicy parse failure → E_POLICY_INVALID → exit 233
--fuel=N—Charged per compiled basic block; exceeding it throws E_FUEL_EXHAUSTEDExit 229
--deadline-ms=N—Wall-clock time limit (sampled every 1024 blocks + at FFI/builtin boundaries)Exit 230
--mem-cap-bytes=N—Byte limit for the VM execution allocator (0 = unlimited)Exit 231
--max-call-depth=N—Guest recursion depth limit; 0 is not allowedDefault 100000; when exceeded, the TEB host-stack gate (256 KiB headroom) is also applied → E_STACK_OVERFLOW → exit 235

If parsing of any numeric flag fails, Invalid value for --xxx: yyy is immediately printed to stderr and the process exits 1. An unrecognized --xxx exits 1 and prints Unknown vm option: xxx.

Exit Codes and Boundaries

The order in which exit codes are generated (consistent with the control flow of src/plugin.zig::runVmCommand):

  1. Argument errors (including misaligned usage, unknown flag, missing file path, flag missing a value, invalid numeric value): exit 1.
  2. Source read / preprocessing / parsing / FFI loading failure: exit 1.
  3. Invalid policy: E_POLICY_INVALID → 233.
  4. --sandboxed used together with --policy / --allow-ffi: E_SANDBOX_MISCONFIG → 234.
  5. Execution-time panic: PANIC[code]: msg is written to stderr, returning 128 + (code & 0x7f).
  6. Sandbox resource violations: E_FUEL_EXHAUSTED → 229, E_TIMEOUT → 230, E_MEM_QUOTA → 231, E_STACK_OVERFLOW → 235, E_CAPABILITY_DENIED → 228.
  7. Normal return: the return integer of @main (truncated to u8).

Environment Variables

All variables are read by the plugin host and the vm implementation in the following order; unset is treated as not set.

VariablePurposeTypical value
SA_PLUGIN_DEVAllows loading the local libvm.so pointed to by SA_PLUGINS_PATH, skipping the sandbox permissions.lock check1
SA_PLUGINS_PATHAbsolute path to the local vm shared library$PWD/zig-out/lib/libvm.so
SA_CACHERoot directory of the vm persistent preprocessing cacheAny writable absolute path
SA_VM_POLICYFalls back to this file when --policy is not explicitly givenPolicy JSON path
SA_VM_FUELFallback fuelDecimal integer
SA_VM_DEADLINE_MSFallback wall-clock limit (ms)Decimal integer
SA_VM_MEM_CAP_BYTESFallback memory limit (bytes)Decimal integer
SA_VM_DISABLE_CALL_CACHEDisables the call cache1 disables it
SA_VM_DISABLE_TAIL_RESTARTDisables tail self-call restart1 disables it
SA_VM_DISABLE_BLOCK_FASTPATHDisables the basic-block fast arm1 disables it
SA_VM_DISABLE_INTERPRETED_FASTPATHDisables the interpreted-function fast path1 disables it
SA_VM_DISABLE_PREPROCESS_CACHEDisables the persistent preprocessing cache1 disables it
SA_VM_DISABLE_PARSE_CACHEDisables the in-process parse cache LRU1 disables it
NoteSA_VM_POLICY / SA_VM_FUEL / SA_VM_DEADLINE_MS / SA_VM_MEM_CAP_BYTES are all filled in after explicit CLI flags: “an explicit CLI flag overrides env, env overrides the limits inside the policy”. See the Resource Limits and Exit Codes page for details.

Complete Copyable Examples

Simplest Local Development Invocation

SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 SA_PLUGINS_PATH="$PWD/zig-out/lib/libvm.so" \
    sa vm run tests/hello_world.sa

With Execution Statistics

SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 SA_PLUGINS_PATH="$PWD/zig-out/lib/libvm.so" \
    sa vm run --stats app.sa

The output is written to stderr, in the form:

VM stats:
  preprocess_ns=...
  preprocess_cache=hit|miss|disabled
  parse_ns=...
  parse_cache=hit|miss|disabled|clone_failed|store_failed
  ffi_load_ns=...
  bind_ns=...
  execute_ns=...
  total_ns=...
  function_calls=...
  interpreted_calls=...
  bytecode_ops=...
  slow_ops=...
  fast_block_hits=...
  tail_restarts=...
  call_cache_hits=...
  call_cache_misses=...
  call_cache_stores=...
  call_cache_clears=...
  frame_pool_hits=...
  frame_pool_misses=...
  frame_pool_releases=...
  memory_epoch_bumps=...
  max_call_depth=...

Top 10 Function Profile

SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 SA_PLUGINS_PATH="$PWD/zig-out/lib/libvm.so" \
    sa vm run --profile=10 app.sa

Appended after everything in --stats:

VM profile top 10:
  @fib calls=... total_ns=... avg_ns=...
  ...

Sandbox: Fixture + Resource Limits + Policy

SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 SA_PLUGINS_PATH="$PWD/zig-out/lib/libvm.so" \
    sa vm run --fuel=1000000 --deadline-ms=5000 \
    --mem-cap-bytes=134217728 --max-call-depth=50000 \
    --policy policy.json tests/fibonacci.sa

SAB Bytecode

SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 SA_PLUGINS_PATH="$PWD/zig-out/lib/libvm.so" \
    sa vm run build/app.sab

vm recognizes SAB files via the "SAB\x00" magic and reuses loadProgram from src/sab_loader.zig to rebuild a Program of the same shape as the text parsing path, with no need to go through preprocessing again.

@test Mode

SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 SA_PLUGINS_PATH="$PWD/zig-out/lib/libvm.so" \
    sa vm test tests/vm_test_mode.sa

Isolated Sandbox (Deny Every Unlisted extern)

SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 SA_PLUGINS_PATH="$PWD/zig-out/lib/libvm.so" \
    sa vm run --sandboxed tests/sandboxed.sa

Disable Optimizations One by One (Debug Tool)

SA_VM_DISABLE_CALL_CACHE=1           sa vm run --stats app.sa
SA_VM_DISABLE_TAIL_RESTART=1         sa vm run --stats app.sa
SA_VM_DISABLE_BLOCK_FASTPATH=1       sa vm run --stats app.sa
SA_VM_DISABLE_INTERPRETED_FASTPATH=1 sa vm run --stats app.sa
SA_VM_DISABLE_PREPROCESS_CACHE=1     sa vm run --stats app.sa
SA_VM_DISABLE_PARSE_CACHE=1          sa vm run --stats app.sa

Common Misconceptions

  • Running a .sa file as if it were .sab: vm looks at the first 4 bytes, not the extension; misplaced bytecode is rejected with SAB loading failed.
  • Writing the wrong schema in the --policy file: it is recognized as not sa.vm.policy/1, yielding E_POLICY_INVALID → 233, and there is no start line in the event stream — execution never started.
  • Relying on SA_CACHE while forgetting its fallback path when it is not set: vm automatically uses $HOME/.cache/sa/vm/preprocess.
